subject: science
title: How Things Move
about: The ways things move (straight, zigzag, round and round, back and forth, up and down, fast and slow), what changes that motion (a ramp, a wall, a harder push) and the position words that tell where a thing is (PS.1.1.1, PS.1.1.2). NC's forces objective has children describe motion and position before they explain it.
tip: Roll a toy car down a book propped on a pillow, then on a taller stack, and ask him to say how it moved each time: straight, fast, slow, down.

cards.q: You roll a ball across a flat floor. How does it move?
cards.note: A rolling ball goes straight until something pushes it a new way.

cards.q: A rabbit runs this way, then that way, then this way again. How does it move?
cards.note: Zigzag means turning from side to side as you go.

cards.q: You ride a merry-go-round. How does it move?
cards.note: A spinning top and a bike wheel go round and round too.

cards.q: You sit on a swing. It goes out, then back, then out again. How does it move?
cards.note: A rocking chair and a seesaw go back and forth too.

cards.q: You bounce a ball. Which way does it go?
cards.note: Down to the floor, back up to your hand, again and again.

cards.q: A race car zooms past. Is it moving fast or slow?
cards.note: Fast and slow tell how quickly something moves.

cards.q: A snail creeps along a leaf. Is it moving fast or slow?
cards.note: Slow is still moving. Not moving at all is called still.

cards.q: You let go of a toy car at the top of a ramp. Which way does it roll?
cards.note: Things roll down a ramp on their own. You have to push to send one up.

cards.q: One ramp is tall and one is low. Which ramp makes the car roll faster?
cards.note: A taller, steeper ramp makes the car go faster and farther.

cards.q: A rolling ball hits a wall. What happens to the ball?
cards.note: The wall pushes back on the ball. Sometimes the ball bounces back a little.

cards.q: Your toy car stopped too soon. How do you make it roll farther next time?
cards.note: A bigger push makes a thing go faster and farther.

cards.q: A balloon floats up over your head. Where is the balloon?
cards.note: Above means higher than. Position words tell where a thing is.

cards.q: Your shoes are on the floor under your bed. Where are the shoes?
cards.note: Below means lower than. Under and beneath mean the same thing.

cards.q: Your cup is right next to your plate. Which word tells where the cup is?
You hide at the back of the couch where nobody can see you. Where are you?
cards.note: Behind means at the back of.

cards.q: A dog sits between you and the TV, so you cannot see the screen. Where is the dog?
cards.note: In front of is the opposite of behind.

cards.q: A ball is on the chair. You move it to the floor. What changed about the ball?
cards.note: Position means where a thing is. A push or a pull can change it.
